Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q2 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premiums growth across our lines of business, elevated policy retention rates reflecting our customer-centric approach, the positive impact of our disciplined pricing changes on premium volume, and a well-balanced asset allocation strategy generating solid investment income.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $525 million, or $2.18 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included premium expansion from rate adequacy and retention gains, alongside favorable claims trends and investment returns. Our combined ratio was 94.2%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with a risk-based capital ratio of 452%.

Before I dive deeper into the segment results, let me highlight our net written premiums—or NWP—performance, which grew 9.2% year-over-year to $4.8 billion. This marks our strongest quarterly NWP growth in three years, driven by disciplined rate actions across the book, improved retention rates averaging 89.5%, and robust new business flows with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.15x. Excluding the impacts from our strategic exit of underperforming California wildfire exposure—down $150 million in NWP—we delivered organic growth of 10.1%, outpacing the industry average of 7.5% as reported by AM Best.

Let me break this down by line of business, with some color on the drivers, regional dynamics, and our forward initiatives.

Personal Lines saw +7.8% NWP growth to $1.9 billion. Personal Lines continues to be our growth engine, benefiting from persistent rate adequacy amid elevated repair costs—inflation in auto parts and labor is still running at 12-15% year-over-year, per CCC Intelligent Solutions data. Auto premiums grew 6.2%, with earned rate of 8.1% offsetting a modest 1.5% decline in policies-in-force due to heightened competition in Florida and Texas from players like Progressive and GEICO. Our telematics program, ApexDrive, now penetrates 42% of our auto book—up from 28% last year—delivering 15% better loss ratios through usage-based pricing and now integrating IoT data from partnered EV manufacturers like Rivian.

Homeowners surged 10.4%, fueled by 9.2% earned rate and strong retention in the Midwest and Southeast, where we've layered on parametric covers for wind and hail. Regionally, U.S. Northeast growth was 12%, but we saw softer 4% in California after our 20% rate filing approval and non-renewal of 50,000 high-risk policies amid reinsurance capacity constraints. Internationally, our UK personal lines via Apex London grew 11%, capitalizing on hardening motor rates post the FCA's pricing reform.

Commercial Lines delivered +12.5% NWP growth to $1.6 billion. Commercial P&C was the standout, reflecting our focus on middle-market accounts with strong underwriting margins. Workers' Compensation jumped 14.2%, with 11% earned rate and new business up 18%—we're gaining share from Travelers in construction and manufacturing, where payroll inflation has supported rate adequacy. Our combined ratio here improved 220 basis points to 92.6%, thanks to proactive return-to-work programs and AI-driven claims triage reducing medical severity by 8%.

General Liability and Umbrella grew 11.8%, driven by excess & surplus appetite in the Northeast, where social inflation remains a tailwind—litigation funding trends are pushing settlement values up 20% per Jury Verdict Research. Property Commercial was up 13.1%, but tempered by catastrophe losses from Hurricane Beryl; we mitigated via 35% quota share reinsurance with Swiss Re, ceding $220 million. Regionally, Asia-Pacific ex-Japan added 16% via our Singapore hub, targeting supply chain risks in semiconductors.

Specialty Lines achieved +15.3% NWP growth to $850 million. This high-margin segment continues to outperform, with cyber premiums up 22% to $320 million—now 38% of the book—amid surging ransomware attacks, as seen in the Change Healthcare breach. We've expanded capacity through our Lloyd's syndicate, writing directors & officers (D&O) for tech IPOs and cyber for mid-market fintechs, with attachment points averaging $50 million. Environmental and trade credit lines grew 12%, benefiting from global trade tensions and our parametric triggers modeled on Bloomberg commodity indices. Europe contributed 40% of new business here, with GDPR compliance driving demand.

Life & Annuity posted +3.2% NWP growth to $450 million. Life was more measured at +2.8%, reflecting competitive pressures in term life from Prudential and Northwestern Mutual, but our indexed universal life (IUL) products gained traction with 5% rate upside from equity market gains. Annuities accelerated 6.1% to $180 million, fueled by fixed indexed offerings yielding 5.2% crediting rates—our runoff block from the 2022 Voya acquisition is now fully integrated, boosting statutory reserves efficiency. Health supplements grew 4% in the U.S. Medicare Advantage corridor, partnering with Humana for bolt-on dental/vision riders.

Overall, our NWP trajectory underscores portfolio optimization: we've shifted 8% of gross premiums into specialty from legacy auto, targeting ROE expansion to 14% by year-end. Key initiatives include rolling out ApexAI Underwriter platform—leveraging machine learning on 500 million historical claims for real-time pricing, already shaving 10% off manual review times. Regionally, we're doubling down on APAC with a $200 million capital deployment for cyber and parametric products, hedging U.S. cat exposure via cat bond issuances totaling $500 million this year through our Bermuda SPV.

Retention is the lifeblood of our book of business here at Apex Insurance. It directly impacts our lifetime value per policyholder, reduces customer acquisition costs—which averaged just 15% of first-year premiums this quarter—and supports our mid-teens ROE target. Our overall retention rate came in at 88.7% for the quarter, up 110 basis points year-over-year and marking our 11th straight quarter of sequential improvement.

Breaking this down by our major product lines, with some color on the drivers, trends, and strategic levers we're pulling:

Personal Auto retention stood at 89.2%, up 140 basis points year-over-year. Personal auto remains our largest line, representing 42% of in-force premiums. We delivered our strongest quarterly retention in five years at 89.2%, outperforming peers like Progressive, who reported 87.5% in their last print. This uplift was fueled by our expanded Snapshot telematics program, now active with 28% of our policies—up from 19% a year ago. Usage-based insurance (UBI) customers are retaining at 94%, a 300 basis points premium to our book average, thanks to personalized discounts averaging 22% off base rates for safe drivers.

Regionally, we're seeing divergence: Northeast retention hit 91% amid softer catastrophe losses from fewer named storms, while California dipped to 86% due to ongoing wildfire risk and regulatory pressures from Prop 103 rate filings. Our strategic push here includes AI-driven risk segmentation, which allowed us to non-renew just 2.1% of our highest-loss-ratio policies—down from 3.8% last year—while growing policies in force by 4.2%.

Homeowners retention strengthened to 92.1%, up 80 basis points year-over-year, comprising 28% of premiums. Bundling with auto continues to be a powerhouse, with bundled households retaining at 96.5%—a 450 basis points uplift. We saw particular strength in the Midwest at 94%, where benign weather and our HomeGuard smart home IoT integration (now in 15% of policies) reduced claims frequency by 12%.

Conversely, Florida and Texas faced headwinds from hurricane and hail exposure, with retention at 88% and 90%, respectively. Here, we've layered in climate-resilient underwriting models using satellite imagery and third-party peril data from RMS and Karen Clark & Company, trimming our coastal exposure by 7% without sacrificing top-line growth. This discipline helped us hold the line on loss ratios at 62%, versus industry averages creeping toward 68%.

Commercial Property & Casualty (P&C) retention held at 85.4%, flat year-over-year, at 22% of premiums. While flat year-over-year, this masks underlying progress: small business retention improved to 87%, driven by our digital servicing portal, which boasts a 92% Net Promoter Score and reduced mid-term cancellations by 18%. Middle-market accounts, however, saw slight pressure at 83% due to inflation-driven premium adequacy challenges in workers' comp and general liability.

Regionally, the Southeast outperformed at 88% on stronger economic tailwinds, while the industrial Midwest lagged at 82% amid supply chain disruptions elevating business interruption claims. Our response? Targeted account-based pricing with machine learning models incorporating Verisk analytics, which improved rate achievement to 102%—up from 98% last year. We're also piloting cyber endorsements bundled with P&C, boosting retention in that high-growth segment by 5 points.

Life & Annuity retention continues to shine at 95.3%, up 50 basis points year-over-year, reflecting sticky persistency in term life (96.8%) and indexed universal life products for our 8% of premiums block. Lapse rates remain below 2%, well ahead of LIMRA industry benchmarks of 4-5%. This quarter's gain came from enhanced policyholder engagement via our myApex app, with digital policy reviews up 35% year-over-year, and targeted no-lapse guarantee riders that reduced early terminations in the under-50 demographic.

No major regional variances here, but we're leaning into affinity partnerships—like our deal with AARP for seniors—to drive cross-sell into health supplements, where combined retention exceeds 97%.

Across the board, these retention gains underscore our 'Customer First, Risk Smart' framework. We've invested $150 million in tech this year alone—telematics, AI underwriting, and omnichannel servicing—to personalize experiences and optimize portfolios. Compared to peers, our 88.7% overall beats the composite personal lines average of 86% per JD Power, positioning us for 3-5% organic growth in 2024.

That said, we're vigilant on macro risks: rising interest rates are pressuring variable annuities, and catastrophe normalization could test homeowners. Our plan? Double down on data flywheels—integrating Experian credit signals with internal telematics for 10-15% better predictability—and expand bundling incentives, targeting 55% household penetration by year-end. This retention momentum gives us conviction in our full-year guidance: combined ratio at 95.5-96.5%, and EPS growth of 8-10%.

As we unpack the impact of pricing changes on premium volume, which was a key driver of our top-line performance this quarter, we continue to execute on our disciplined pricing strategy amid a hardening market influenced by persistent inflation, elevated catastrophe activity, and rising reinsurance costs—dynamics we've seen across peers like Progressive and Travelers.

Overall, net written premiums grew 6.2% year-over-year to $12.8 billion, reflecting the successful navigation of pricing actions that delivered an average earned rate increase of 8.4% across our book. This was partially offset by a 2.1% decline in policy count volume, as expected in a rate-adequate environment. Our book yield—a critical metric we track internally—expanded by 110 basis points to 4.2%, underscoring improved profitability per policy. This balance allowed us to maintain premium growth while advancing our combined ratio to 92.4%, down 180 points from last year.

In personal lines, which represent 65% of our in-force premium, we implemented targeted rate hikes averaging 9.2%—higher than our initial guidance of 7-8%—driven by auto repair inflation (up 12% year-over-year per CCC Intelligent Solutions data) and homeowners' exposure to secondary perils like hail and wildfire. Personal auto premiums rose 7.5% to $5.2 billion, with earned rates up 10.1% but policy volume down 2.8%, primarily due to non-renewals in high-loss California and Florida markets where we capped writings at 85% of capacity to protect rate adequacy. Homeowners saw even stronger pricing momentum, with a 11.3% rate increase leading to 5.1% premium growth to $3.1 billion, despite a 1.5% volume dip. Retention held steady at 86.5%, bolstered by our ApexDrive telematics program, which now covers 28% of auto policies and segments risks more granularly, enabling 15-20% better pricing precision for safe drivers.

Shifting to commercial lines, which grew premiums 4.8% to $4.5 billion, pricing changes were more nuanced. We achieved an average 6.7% earned rate increase—aligning with industry benchmarks from AM Best—amid softening in middle-market workers' comp but firming in excess & surplus (E&S). Policy volume was flat, but new business submissions surged 12% thanks to our AI-powered underwriting platform, Apollo AI, which integrates satellite imagery and climate risk models from RMS to quote E&S risks 40% faster. This initiative not only supported volume stability but also reduced expense ratio by 50 basis points through automation. In specialty lines like cyber insurance, where we've seen 25%+ rate hikes industry-wide post-ransomware waves, our premiums jumped 18%, outpacing Chubb and AIG.

Regionally, the story varies significantly. In the U.S., our core market, pricing discipline yielded 7.1% premium growth, with the Southeast (high cat exposure) seeing 10.2% rate increases to offset $450 million in Hurricane Idalia attritional losses. Conversely, the Midwest benefited from milder weather, allowing 3% volume expansion alongside 7% pricing. Internationally, Europe contributed 8% growth to $1.9 billion in premiums, driven by 9.5% rates in UK motor amid inflation-linked repairs (per Thatcham Research), though volume softened 1.2% due to competitive pressures from Direct Line. In Asia-Pacific, our joint venture with Ping An delivered 12% premium growth on 11% rates, fueled by expansion in usage-based insurance for two-wheelers in India, where penetration is now at 15% of policies.

Strategically, these pricing changes are not opportunistic but rooted in our Rate on Line (ROL) optimization framework, which targets 5-7% annual adequacy to outpace loss trends. We've layered in advanced analytics—partnering with Eagle Alpha for alternative data on social inflation—to dynamically adjust rates weekly in volatile lines. This has de-risked our portfolio: catastrophe loss ratio improved to 4.2% from 6.1%, and our reinsurance tower, renewed at July 1 with a 15% cost increase, now features higher attachments via sidecars totaling $1.2 billion from third-party capital like Stone Ridge.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 earned rates of 7-9% with premium growth of 5-7%, assuming normalized cats. We'll continue pruning underperforming books—targeting a 2-3% volume contraction in personal lines if loss trends persist—while scaling new business in high-ROL segments like parametric insurance for climate risks. This positions us for sustained ROE expansion above our 15% target.

I'll now turn to our investment portfolio performance and asset allocation strategy, which remains a cornerstone of our ability to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns while supporting our long-tail liabilities across life, P&C, and annuity lines. Our general account invested assets stood at $258 billion at quarter-end, up 4% year-over-year, reflecting strong premium growth and positive operating cash flows from our core insurance operations.

Our portfolio is rigorously managed through our Asset Liability Management (ALM) framework, with a keen focus on duration matching—currently at 7.2 years for our life reserves versus a portfolio duration of 7.1 years—and convexity hedging via interest rate swaps and Treasury futures to mitigate basis risk in a volatile rate environment. We've maintained our target risk budget, with economic capital allocation under Solvency II and NAIC RBC metrics comfortably above 500% thresholds.

Fixed Income comprises 74% of the portfolio, or $191 billion. This remains our bedrock, providing stable, predictable income to match our actuarial liabilities, particularly in our universal life and long-term care blocks. The sleeve breakdown is as follows: Investment-grade corporates: 42% ($80 billion), with a yield-to-worst of 4.8%. We've leaned into BBB-rated credits from sectors like utilities and financials—think names like NextEra Energy and Wells Fargo—where spreads have tightened to 140bps over Treasuries amid the post-2022 rate normalization. Our credit quality is pristine, with 92% IG and an average rating of A-. U.S. Treasuries and agency MBS: 28% ($53 billion), yielding 4.2% blended. We've extended duration here slightly to 8.1 years, capitalizing on the 2023 bond rally, while using CMBS IO strips for enhanced carry without undue extension risk. RMBS and CLOs: 4% ($8 billion), focused on seasoned, performing loans with low delinquency rates under 1.5%.

Regionally, 65% is U.S.-centric for liquidity and regulatory matching under VM-20, 20% Eurozone sovereigns and Pfandbriefe for yield pickup in a sub-3% ECB environment, and 15% in high-quality Asian credits like Singapore gilts. Yields compressed 25bps quarter-over-quarter, but our book yield held steady at 4.6% thanks to disciplined reinvestment—$12 billion deployed this quarter at 5.1% new money rates.

Equities represent 13% of the portfolio, or $34 billion. We've held this sleeve steady, balancing growth potential against volatility. Public equities make up 9% ($23 billion), benchmarked to a custom 60/40 S&P 500/International blend, delivering 8.2% YTD returns driven by tech and financials—holdings include Microsoft and JPMorgan. Private equities are 4% ($11 billion), via limited partner commitments to funds like KKR and Carlyle, targeting 12-15% IRRs with a focus on insurance-adjacent buyouts in healthcare services.

Strategically, we're de-risking via covered call overlays on 30% of the public book, generating an extra 80bps of income while capping upside in this high-valuation market (S&P forward P/E at 21x). Regional mix: 55% U.S., 25% Europe (STOXX 600 exposure), and 20% emerging markets, with a tilt to India via Nifty 50 ETFs amid 7% GDP growth forecasts.

Alternatives account for 13% of the portfolio, or $33 billion. This is where we're driving alpha in a low-for-long yield world, up from 10% two years ago as we rotate out of duration-sensitive bonds. Real assets (real estate and infrastructure): 6% ($15 billion), yielding 6.8% net. Key positions include core-plus office conversions in Sunbelt markets and renewables via partnerships with Brookfield—$2 billion in solar and wind farms, aligned with our TCFD climate disclosures and generating 50bps ESG premium. Private credit and direct lending: 4% ($10 billion), at 9.2% blended yield through club deals with Ares and Owl Rock, focusing on middle-market sponsors in a Fed funds rate regime above 5%. Hedge strategies: 3% ($8 billion), portable alpha via multi-strat funds from Citadel and Millennium, returning 7.5% YTD with low beta to equities.

We've initiated a $5 billion tactical allocation to insurance-linked securities (ILS), including cat bonds on our own Florida hurricane book via Everest Re, achieving 6-8% yields with zero correlation to public markets. Regionally, 40% U.S. infra for IIJA tailwinds, 30% European social housing, and 30% APAC digital infra.

Portfolio yield expanded to 5.1% from 4.7% last year, outpacing the Bloomberg Aggregate's 4.3%, while volatility (tracking error) remains under 75bps. In response to persistent inflation—core PCE at 2.7%—we've boosted inflation-linked bonds to 5% of fixed income ($9.5 billion), hedging our P&C inflation sensitivities. Technologically, our ALICO platform—powered by BlackRock's Aladdin—has optimized $20 billion in rebalancing this year, reducing transaction costs by 15% via ML-driven scenario analysis under our Economic Capital Model.

Looking forward, with the Fed eyeing 25bps cuts in H2 2024, we're positioning for a barbell: extending high-quality duration while scaling alternatives to 15% by year-end. This supports our 8-10% ROE target, funds $15 billion in share repurchases, and bolsters our 22x embedded value multiple versus peers like MetLife or Prudential. Risks are well-hedged—Greek risk at 1.2% VaR—and we're advancing our net-zero by 2050 pathway with $10 billion in sustainable assets.

We guide full-year NWP growth of 8-10%, assuming mid-single-digit earned rates and stable reinsurance costs—our Q3 renewal with Munich Re locked in flat terms. Risks include persistent inflation and secondary perils, but our 75% retention and 1.12x book-to-bill position us well against peers.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for participating in the question-and-answer session will be given momentarily. Our first question comes from David Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Chen: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the NWP growth in specialty lines, particularly cyber, and how you're managing ransomware risks?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. Elena and Michael have been leading our specialty push. Cyber grew 22% as ransomware threats like the Change Healthcare incident have heightened demand. We're expanding via our Lloyd's syndicate, focusing on mid-market fintechs and tech IPO D&O, with strong attachment points. Underwriting discipline keeps loss ratios tight, and our ApexAI platform helps price risks in real-time.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent catastrophe activity, like Hurricane Beryl, on your business and outlook?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Lisa. Cats tempered some property growth, but our mitigation—35% quota share with Swiss Re ceding $220 million—kept the combined ratio in check. We've trimmed high-risk exposures and issued $500 million in cat bonds via our Bermuda SPV. Full-year cat loss assumption in guidance is conservative, supporting our 95.5-96.5% combined ratio target.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Thanks. On retention, how sustainable are the gains in personal auto, and any updates on telematics penetration?

Elena Vasquez: Hi, Robert. 89.2% retention in auto is driven by ApexDrive at 42% penetration, with UBI customers at 94%. We're seeing 22% discounts for safe drivers boosting loyalty. AI segmentation minimized non-renewals to 2.1%, and we'll target 50% telematics by year-end for further uplift.

Operator: Our next question is from Emily Torres with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Torres: Good morning. Regarding asset allocation, what's your view on alternatives scaling to 15%, and any shift due to potential rate cuts?

Michael Rivera: Morning, Emily. Alternatives at 13% are yielding alpha—real assets at 6.8%, private credit at 9.2%, plus new ILS. With Fed cuts eyed, our barbell extends duration in IG while growing alts. ALICO optimizes this, keeping tracking error low under 75bps, supporting ROE above 8-10%.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
